name: NVIDIA Corporation
description: Research target. NVIDIA designs GPUs and accelerated-computing platforms for AI training/inference, data centers, gaming, and automotive. Fabless: relies on foundries and contract manufacturers.

name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC)
description: World's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry; primary manufacturing partner for NVIDIA's most advanced GPUs (wafer fabrication).

name: SK Hynix Inc.
description: Leading memory maker; primary supplier of HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) used in NVIDIA AI accelerators.

name: Micron Technology, Inc.
description: US memory manufacturer; named by NVIDIA in its 10-K as a memory supplier.

name: ASML Holding N.V.
description: Sole producer of EUV lithography machines. Indirect supplier: sells to foundries (TSMC, Samsung, Intel) that manufacture for NVIDIA; not a direct NVIDIA vendor.

name: Microsoft Corporation
description: Largest estimated customer of NVIDIA data-center GPUs (Omdia/Bloomberg estimates); also a strategic partner (Azure AI, NVIDIA partnership).

name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
description: Major AI infrastructure spender; second-largest estimated NVIDIA GPU customer after Microsoft (Omdia estimates).

name: Amazon.com, Inc.
description: Hyperscaler running NVIDIA GPUs in AWS; estimated top-4 NVIDIA customer. Also develops custom chips (Trainium/Inferentia), partially competing with NVIDIA.

name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
description: Google Cloud and Google TPU developer; estimated top-4 NVIDIA customer while also building custom accelerators.

name: Dell Technologies Inc.
description: Leading OEM of NVIDIA-powered AI servers (AI Factory initiative with NVIDIA); major channel customer for enterprise AI.

name: Accenture plc
description: Global professional services firm; strategic partner running an NVIDIA Business Group (30,000 trained professionals) around the AI Refinery platform.

name: ServiceNow, Inc.
description: Enterprise workflow AI platform; expanded strategic partnership with NVIDIA to co-develop agentic AI (NVIDIA NIM Agent Blueprints).

name: Snowflake Inc.
description: Data Cloud company; partnership with NVIDIA to run NVIDIA NeMo on the Snowflake platform for enterprise generative AI.

name: Cisco Systems, Inc.
description: Networking leader; partner on 'Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA' and co-developer of NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet-based switches (N9100 series).

name: CoreWeave, Inc.
description: GPU-cloud provider; NVIDIA invested $100M (2023) and $2B (2026), and is its largest GPU supplier. CoreWeave builds AI data centers for NVIDIA.

name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
description: AI-driven drug discovery company; NVIDIA invested $50M (July 2023) and collaborates on foundation models and DGX Cloud compute (BioHive supercomputer).

name: SoundHound AI, Inc.
description: Voice-AI company. NVIDIA participated in its 2017 $75M funding round but disclosed selling its stake in February 2025 — a now-expired investment relationship.

name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD)
description: Primary direct competitor in data-center GPUs and AI accelerators (MI-series). Named in NVIDIA's 10-K as a competitor.

name: Intel Corporation
description: Competitor in CPUs, AI accelerators (Gaudi) and emerging foundry services. Named in NVIDIA's 10-K as a competitor.

name: Broadcom Inc.
description: Competitor in data-center networking (DPUs, switches) and custom AI ASIC design for hyperscalers. Named in NVIDIA's 10-K.

name: Qualcomm Incorporated
description: Competitor in edge/automotive/SoC computing. Named in NVIDIA's 10-K as a competitor in embedded and automotive devices.
